oil.summary: Crude markets are sending mixed signals heading into the close. WTI slipped 0.91% to $75.08 while Brent held near flat at $79.40, masking a brutal week that has shaved more than 11% off both benchmarks. The geopolitical tape remains intensely active: Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea, Ukraine struck a Russian airbase and refinery, and Iran maintained its oil blockade as Trump threatened further escalation. Against that backdrop, Aramco posted record Q2 profits tied to the Iran war supply squeeze, though analysts flag a growing underlying cash flow concern. Offsetting bearish pressure, a potential interim Hormuz deal reportedly awaits Khamenei's signature, which may explain why any upside is being capped. Indian refiners are pivoting to Omani and West African grades as Mideast term supply tightens. US crude inventories rose 2.5 million barrels last week, but product stocks continued to draw.
drivers: Houthi ballistic missile strike on Saudi tanker in Red Sea escalates physical supply-route risk
Iran blockade/Hormuz deal uncertainty: draft agreement reportedly awaiting Khamenei approval, capping both downside and upside
US crude stocks built 2.5 mb but product inventories fell, with Indian refiners shifting to West African and Omani grades amid Mideast disruption

gas.summary: Natural gas markets showed a sharp divergence today. Henry Hub eased another 0.45% to $2.67/MMBtu, extending a painful 18% monthly slide that points to soft domestic fundamentals. TTF in Europe dropped a sharper 4.43% to €53.445/MWh on the day, though TTF remains up nearly 15% over the past month, reflecting lingering Hormuz-linked LNG supply anxiety that is now partially unwinding on Hormuz deal optimism. Headlines were sparse on gas-specific fundamentals; the dominant story remains geopolitical. The US is reportedly targeting a Wednesday announcement on an interim Hormuz deal, and Iraq is exploring a Syria pipeline bypass that could redirect Gulf flows within three years. India is also weighing a gas levy to fund a $42 billion fuel reserve plan, a longer-term demand signal.
drivers: Henry Hub continues its steep monthly decline (-18.22%), reflecting weak US domestic fundamentals
TTF sold off sharply (-4.43% on the day) as Hormuz deal optimism reduces European LNG supply-risk premium
India's proposed gas levy for a $42 billion strategic reserve signals medium-term demand growth; Iraq-Syria pipeline bypass emerges as a multi-year Hormuz alternative

power.summary: Power and carbon markets were relatively quiet on price action today. EU EUAs edged down just 0.12% to $77.02, essentially flat on the week (-0.85%) and marginally positive on the month (+1.36%), offering little directional conviction. The dominant news touching the power sector is geopolitical: a drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant (reported yesterday) briefly lifted oil to a two-week high, underlining vulnerability of regional power infrastructure. Separately, a Hormuz draft agreement reportedly awaits Khamenei approval, and if confirmed could ease the LNG and fuel-oil supply pressure that has been indirectly supporting carbon prices by incentivising coal burn in Europe. A Senate sanctions push targeting Russian energy financing and China exposure adds another layer of medium-term supply uncertainty. News flow specific to European power and carbon fundamentals was thin today.
drivers: Drone attack on UAE nuclear plant highlights regional power-infrastructure vulnerability and briefly supported risk premium across energy complexes
Hormuz draft deal awaiting Khamenei approval: ratification could ease LNG tightness and reduce indirect support for EUA prices via lower coal-switching incentives
Senate push for new sanctions on Russian energy financing and China exposure introduces additional medium-term uncertainty for European gas and carbon markets
